# k0rdent_network (Resource)

A tenant fabric network: an Ethernet (EVPN), InfiniBand or NVLink segment that subnets are allocated inside.

Exactly one of `evpn`, `infiniband` or `nvlink` must be set, and it is the one that decides the network's `type`. Everything except `display_name`, `description` and `tags` is immutable: the API offers no way to change a fabric in place, so a change anywhere else replaces the network.

Networks materialized by a cluster are not managed here. They carry a `cluster_id`, and the tenant API answers `409` to any write against them.

Requires `region` and `project` on the provider.

**What replaces it.** Changing `evpn`, `id`, `infiniband`, `nvlink`, `project` or `region` cannot be done in place and replaces the network. A network carries the subnets and interfaces tenant workloads attach to, and a replacement deletes it and allocates a new fabric segment. So a plan that would replace it fails and names the attribute, unless `allow_replace = true` is set on the resource. Everything else changes in place.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An Ethernet fabric. The `evpn`, `infiniband` or `nvlink` block picks the kind.
resource "k0rdent_network" "training" {
  id           = "training-fabric"
  display_name = "Training fabric"

  # Merged with the provider's `default_tags` into `tags_all`. These win.
  tags = {
    team = "ml-platform"
  }

  evpn = {
    service_type = "l3vpn"
    mtu          = 9000
    dns_servers  = ["10.0.0.2", "10.0.0.3"]

    # "auto" lets the platform pick. The chosen id is in `vlan_id_resolved`.
    vlan_id = "auto"
  }
}

# An InfiniBand fabric. Without `pkey`, the platform picks one and reports it
# in `pkey_allocated`.
resource "k0rdent_network" "gpu_interconnect" {
  id = "gpu-interconnect"

  infiniband = {
    partition  = "training"
    ip_over_ib = true
  }
}

# An NVLink fabric. With no partition named, the fabric picks one.
resource "k0rdent_network" "nvlink" {
  id     = "nvlink-domain"
  nvlink = {}
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `allow_replace` (Boolean) Permit a plan that replaces this network. Left out or `false`, a change that cannot be made in place fails the plan, naming the attribute that forces the replacement, instead of destroying the network and creating another. Set it to `true` in the same configuration as the change to let the replacement go ahead, and remove it afterwards to put the guard back. It is read from the configuration being planned and must be known at plan time. It is never sent to the platform: setting or removing it on its own is an update that changes nothing there.
- `description` (String) Free-form text describing it, for people to read.
- `display_name` (String) Human-friendly name. One of three mutable fields.
- `evpn` (Attributes) An Ethernet fabric network. Sets `type` to `evpn`. **Can force replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`): replaces the network unless the only difference is a `vlan_id` the allocated id satisfies. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--evpn))
- `id` (String) Network name, and the id this resource is imported by. Omit it and the provider generates one, `tf-` and 16 hex digits, so that a create whose answer is lost can be read back rather than sent twice. Cannot be changed after creation. **Forces replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`). **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL. String length must be at most 63.
- `infiniband` (Attributes) An InfiniBand fabric network. Sets `type` to `infiniband`. **Can force replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`): replaces the network, except for a `pkey` an import could not record. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--infiniband))
- `nvlink` (Attributes) An NVLink fabric network. Sets `type` to `nvlink`. Write `nvlink = {}` to let the fabric bind the partition itself. **Forces replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--nvlink))
- `project` (String) Project this resource belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project`. It's part of the resource's API path, so a resource can't move between projects. **Forces replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`). **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `region` (String) Region this resource lives in. Defaults to the provider's `region`. It's part of the resource's API path, so a resource can't move between regions. **Forces replacement** (needs `allow_replace = true`). **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `tags` (Map of String) User-defined labels. The platform keeps its own `systemTags` separately and they are not exposed here, so nothing the platform writes can collide with a tag set in configuration. **Constraints:** The key `terraform-provider-k0rdent/create-token` is the provider's own.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) How long each operation may take before it fails. Each operation left out defaults to the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `cluster_id` (String) UID of the cluster that provisioned this network. Present only on networks the cluster lifecycle owns, which cannot be written through this resource. A value here on an imported network means the import was a mistake.
- `self_link` (String) Platform-defined reference to this network.
- `state` (String) Lifecycle state as last read from the platform.
- `tags_all` (Map of String) Every tag the platform holds for this resource: the provider's `default_tags` with this resource's own `tags` on top, a resource tag winning over a default with the same key. Known at plan whenever both are, so the plan shows the result. The provider's create token never appears here.
- `type` (String) `evpn`, `infiniband` or `nvlink`. Derived from which fabric block is set, never written in configuration.
- `vpc` (String) The fabric VPC this network attaches to. Reported only for cluster-provisioned networks.

<a id="nestedatt--evpn"></a>
### Nested Schema for `evpn`

Required:

- `service_type` (String) `l2vpn` for an L2 EVPN fabric, `l3vpn` for an L3 one. **Constraints:** Value must be one of: ["l2vpn" "l3vpn"].

Optional:

- `dhcp_enabled` (Boolean) Whether DHCP serves addresses on this network. Defaults to `false`.
- `dns_servers` (List of String) Resolver addresses, in order. A List rather than a Set because resolver order is significant.
- `mtu` (Number) Maximum transmission unit. The platform applies its own when unset. **Constraints:** Value must be between 68 and 65535.
- `vlan_id` (String) VLAN id as a string, e.g. `"100"`, or `"auto"` to let the platform allocate one. See `vlan_id_resolved` for what it chose. **Constraints:** Must be "auto" or a VLAN number from 1 to 9999 with no leading zero.

Read-Only:

- `vlan_id_resolved` (String) The VLAN id the platform actually assigned. Equal to `vlan_id` unless that was `"auto"`.


<a id="nestedatt--infiniband"></a>
### Nested Schema for `infiniband`

Optional:

- `index0` (Boolean) Store the PKey at index 0. Defaults to `false`.
- `ip_over_ib` (Boolean) Whether the partition takes part in IP-over-InfiniBand multicast. Defaults to `false`.
- `partition` (String) Name of an operator-defined InfiniBand Partition in the region. Required on the `nico` backend. The contract does not gate by backend, so the server decides and this attribute cannot. **Known gap.** No operation in the contract lists partitions, so the name comes from the operator. The [hardcoded values](../guides/hardcoded-values.md) guide names the side that has to change. **Constraints:** String length must be at least 1.
- `pkey` (String) Partition key in hex, e.g. `0x1234`. Omitted, the platform may allocate one. The `nico` backend ignores it and uses the partition name. See `pkey_allocated`. An import cannot recover the requested value, so the first apply after one records the configured value without replacing the network. **Constraints:** Must be 0x and hex digits, such as 0x1234.

Read-Only:

- `pkey_allocated` (String) The PKey the platform reports, whether it was asked for or allocated.


<a id="nestedatt--nvlink"></a>
### Nested Schema for `nvlink`

Optional:

- `partition` (String) Name of an operator-defined NVLink Logical Partition in the region. Omit it and the fabric binds one. **Known gap.** No operation in the contract lists partitions, so the name comes from the operator. The [hardcoded values](../guides/hardcoded-values.md) guide names the side that has to change. **Constraints:** String length must be at least 1.


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) Bounds the whole create, including the wait until the platform reports it ready. Left out, it defaults to the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. **Constraints:** Must be a positive duration of hours, minutes or seconds, such as `45m`, `2h` or `1h30m`.
- `delete` (String) Bounds the whole destroy, including the wait until the platform reports it gone. Left out, it defaults to the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. **Constraints:** Must be a positive duration of hours, minutes or seconds, such as `45m`, `2h` or `1h30m`.
- `update` (String) Bounds the whole update, including the wait until the platform settles. Left out, it defaults to the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. **Constraints:** Must be a positive duration of hours, minutes or seconds, such as `45m`, `2h` or `1h30m`.

## Timeouts

The `timeouts` block sets how long each operation may take before it fails:

- `create` (default `2h`). Bounds the whole create, including the wait until the platform reports it ready.
- `update` (default `2h`). Bounds the whole update, including the wait until the platform settles.
- `delete` (default `2h`). Bounds the whole destroy, including the wait until the platform reports it gone.

Each default is the provider's `operation_timeout`, which is `2h` unless the provider block or `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` sets it. An operation the block leaves out takes that value, so raising `operation_timeout` raises all of them at once. A value of zero or less is refused at plan time rather than read as no limit.

A wait that runs out, or a run that is interrupted, stops nothing on the platform. A create that stops waiting fails, and Terraform taints the object: run `terraform untaint` on it and then `terraform apply`, which waits for the same object. A delete that stops waiting fails and stays in state, and the next `terraform destroy` waits for the same delete without sending another.

```terraform
resource "k0rdent_network" "example" {
  # ...

  timeouts {
    create = "45m"
    update = "45m"
    delete = "45m"
  }
}
```

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# The same address with each part named. Leave out region and project to
# use the provider's.
import {
  to = k0rdent_network.example
  identity = {
    region  = "us-texas-1"
    project = "cp-production"
    id      = "training-fabric"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) The resource's id.

#### Optional

- `project` (String) Project the resource lives in. Defaults to the provider's `project` on import.
- `region` (String) Region the resource lives in. Defaults to the provider's `region` on import.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Takes every id form `terraform import` does. The first command below uses
# the provider's region and project. The second names them, for a network
# outside the provider's region and project.
#
# With vlan_id = "auto", the plan after an import shows an in-place update
# that changes nothing on the platform. An InfiniBand pkey is the same.
import {
  to = k0rdent_network.example
  id = "us-texas-1/cp-production/training-fabric"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import k0rdent_network.example training-fabric

terraform import k0rdent_network.example us-texas-1/cp-production/training-fabric
```
